requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Judge Decoding: Faster Speculative Sampling Requires Going Beyond Model Alignment' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware, inference frameworks (HuggingFace and gpt-fast), quantization, and model parallelism configurations required to reproduce the paper are set up.
GPU hardware and multi-GPU node configuration matching the paper are available and correctly configured.
A single node of NVIDIA H100-SXM5 GPUs is available with at least 8 GPUs, as specified in Appendix B.3 for running Llama-70B and Llama-405B experiments.

verification.spec: Query GPU availability using `nvidia-smi -L` (or torch.cuda.device_count() and torch.cuda.get_device_name(i) for each i). Assert that at least 8 GPUs are visible and that each reports an NVIDIA H100 (SXM5 variant preferred; accept 'H100' substring match). Additionally verify total aggregate GPU memory >= 8 * 80 GiB via torch.cuda.get_device_properties.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to detect and verify CUDA availability, GPU count (at least 8), and compatible NVIDIA driver / CUDA toolkit versions required by PyTorch and gpt-fast on H100 hardware.

verification.spec: Run a script that calls torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count(), and torch.version.cuda; assert cuda available, device_count >= 8, and that nvidia-smi reports H100 GPUs with a driver compatible with the installed CUDA toolkit.

sub_tasks.requirements: The runtime configuration for Llama-3.1-70B experiments uses exactly 2 H100 GPUs for both HuggingFace and gpt-fast benchmarks, as stated in Table 1 and Appendix B.3.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmarking launch script/config for the 70B experiments; assert that tensor-parallel/world size is exactly 2 and that at runtime torch.cuda.device_count() reports >= 2 H100 GPUs used for the 70B runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The runtime configuration for Llama-3.1-405B experiments uses exactly 8 H100 GPUs for both HuggingFace and gpt-fast benchmarks, as stated in Table 1 and Appendix B.3.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmarking launch script/config for the 405B experiments; assert that tensor-parallel/world size is exactly 8 and that at runtime torch.cuda.device_count() reports >= 8 H100 GPUs used for the 405B runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: 8-bit quantization is applied to Llama-70B and Llama-405B so that the models fit on the specified GPU configuration and match the paper's speed benchmark setup.
Code has been implemented that loads Llama-3.1-70B and Llama-3.1-405B target models with 8-bit weight quantization for gpt-fast inference, following Appendix B.3 and Table 1.

verification.spec: Invoke the gpt-fast model-load routine with int8 weight quantization on the converted Llama-3.1-70B checkpoint; assert model loads successfully and that a sample module's weight dtype/quantized-linear class corresponds to int8 quantization. Repeat spot-check for 405B checkpoint if hardware allows.

sub_tasks.requirements: The quantized Llama-405B model successfully loads across 8 H100 GPUs on a single node, and the quantized Llama-70B model successfully loads across 2 H100 GPUs without out-of-memory failures during a 512+512 token inference run.

verification.spec: Launch the gpt-fast tensor-parallel inference entrypoint on 8xH100 for quantized Llama-3.1-405B (and on 2xH100 for 70B) with a 512-input-token prompt and generate 512 output tokens. Assert generation completes without OOM and returns 512 tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Model / tensor parallelism is configured for gpt-fast so that Llama-70B and Llama-405B are sharded across the specified GPU counts.

Code has been implemented to enable gpt-fast's tensor-parallel inference across the specified number of GPUs (2 for 70B, 8 for 405B) for both draft and target models used in speculative and judge decoding.

verification.spec: Inspect the inference launch script and gpt-fast configuration: assert tensor-parallel world_size is settable and equals 2 for 70B runs and 8 for 405B runs, and that torch.distributed is initialized with NCCL backend.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tensor-parallel launch script produces identical greedy generations (token-for-token) across parallel-degree settings for a fixed prompt, confirming correctness of the sharded model configuration.

verification.spec: Run greedy generation for a fixed prompt on Llama-3.1-8B using tensor-parallel degrees 1 and 2 (or 70B with degrees 2 and 4 if feasible). Assert token IDs are identical across TP settings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Standard speculative decoding verification (probability-based acceptance with stochastic fallback) is correctly implemented as described in Section 3.1, providing the baseline against which judge decoding is measured.
The draft-model candidate generation stage of standard speculative decoding is correctly implemented.
Code has been implemented that autoregressively samples M candidate tokens c_1, ..., c_M from the draft model LLM_draft given the current context s, following Eq. (2) of Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Call the drafting routine with a small draft model and a fixed context s and M=5. Assert it returns a length-M sequence of token ids c_1..c_M produced autoregressively (each token conditioned on s plus previously drafted tokens), matching Eq. (2). Verify by re-running the draft model manually one token at a time and confirming identical outputs under greedy decoding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that for each drafted token c_i the corresponding draft-model probability vector q_i over the vocabulary V is retained and made available to the verifier (so that q_i[c_i] can be evaluated during acceptance).

verification.spec: Invoke the drafting function and confirm its return value includes, alongside the M drafted token ids, an (M, V)-shaped tensor of draft probability vectors q_1..q_M. Check that q_i sums to 1 within numerical tolerance and that q_i[c_i] is retrievable and matches the softmax of the draft model's logits at position i.

sub_tasks.requirements: The draft sampling procedure defaults to greedy decoding for the draft (as stated in Section 3.1: 'using any sampling scheme (but usually greedy)') while remaining compatible with stochastic sampling if enabled.

verification.spec: Confirm the draft sampling API accepts a sampling-mode argument (e.g., 'greedy' or temperature/top-p). With default arguments, verify drafted tokens equal argmax of the draft model logits at each step. With temperature>0, verify sampled tokens can differ across seeds, demonstrating stochastic support.

sub_tasks.requirements: The number of draft tokens M is a configurable parameter of the speculative decoding routine, supporting at least the range used in the paper's experiments (including small M in {5,7,10} for the standard baseline and larger M up to 25 for sweeps).

verification.spec: Call the speculative decoding entrypoint with M in {5, 7, 10, 25} and confirm each run completes and internally drafts exactly M candidate tokens per iteration (assert by hooking the draft call or reading logs). No hard-coded restriction on M below 25 should be present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The parallel target-model forward pass over drafted tokens is correctly implemented.

Code has been implemented that runs a single parallel forward pass of the target model LLM_target on (c_1, ..., c_M) conditioned on context s to obtain probability vectors p_1, ..., p_{M+1}, matching the definition in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Given a fixed s and drafted tokens c_1..c_M, call the target-verification routine and confirm it invokes the target model exactly once (assert via forward-count hook) and returns probability tensors p_1..p_{M+1}. Compare against an independent single call to target_model(s + c_1..c_M) followed by softmax; the p_i tensors must match within numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The target forward pass produces one additional probability vector p_{M+1} corresponding to the position after c_M, which is used to sample a bonus token when all M candidates are accepted.

verification.spec: Run one verification pass on drafted tokens c_1..c_M. Assert the returned probability tensor has M+1 rows. Then force a scenario where all M candidates are accepted (e.g., set draft=target to guarantee full acceptance) and confirm the decode loop samples the bonus token from p_{M+1} and appends it, extending output length by M+1 tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: The token-level acceptance/rejection rule from Equation 4 is implemented exactly as specified.
Code has been implemented that unconditionally accepts candidate token c_i whenever p_i[c_i] >= q_i[c_i] (target probability at least as large as draft probability).

verification.spec: Unit test the SD acceptance function: construct synthetic p_i and q_i with p_i[c_i] >= q_i[c_i] and assert the function returns accept=True deterministically (over many RNG seeds, acceptance rate == 1.0).

sub_tasks.requirements: When p_i[c_i] < q_i[c_i], code has been implemented that accepts c_i with probability p_i[c_i]/q_i[c_i] via a Bernoulli draw (the 'biased coin flip' in Section 3.1), and otherwise rejects it.

verification.spec: Unit test the SD acceptance function: for fixed p_i[c_i]=a, q_i[c_i]=b with a<b, run the acceptance decision N=10000 times with different RNG seeds and assert empirical accept rate is within 0.02 of a/b.

sub_tasks.requirements: The verification routine outputs an accept mask z_stand in {0,1}^M whose entries correspond exactly to the per-token acceptance decisions of Eq. (4), and this mask is exposed so that judge decoding can OR it with z_judge.

verification.spec: Invoke the verification routine on a batch of M candidate tokens with known synthetic p and q; assert the routine returns (or exposes) z_stand as a length-M binary tensor whose entries match a reference implementation of Eq. 4 element-wise, and that this mask is accessible to the judge OR-combining code path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that once a token c_i is rejected, all subsequent candidates c_{i+1}, ..., c_M are discarded regardless of their individual accept flags, matching the sequential semantics of standard SD.

verification.spec: Construct a case where a mocked acceptance function forces z_stand=[1,1,0,1,1]; run the SD driver and assert the driver commits only the first 2 candidate tokens (and one corrected token from p_i) to the context, ignoring the later 1s.

sub_tasks.requirements: The corrected-token and bonus-token sampling logic that guarantees at least one produced token per iteration is correctly implemented.

On the first rejection at position i, code has been implemented that samples the replacement token from the residual distribution derived from p_i (the standard SD corrected distribution proportional to max(0, p_i - q_i)), so that the sampled token is drawn from the target distribution.

verification.spec: Given synthetic p_i and q_i and a forced first-rejection at position i, sample the replacement token N=20000 times; assert the empirical distribution of sampled tokens matches the normalized max(0, p_i - q_i) distribution within TV-distance 0.02.

sub_tasks.requirements: When all M candidate tokens are accepted, code has been implemented that samples one additional bonus token from p_{M+1} and appends it to the context, as described in the last paragraph of Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Set up a mock where all M candidate tokens are accepted; run the SD step and assert the returned new tokens has length M+1 and the extra token is sampled from p_{M+1} (verify by checking sampling matches p_{M+1} over many seeds within TV 0.02).

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end SD loop guarantees at least one new token is produced per iteration (via bonus token, accepted candidate, or resampled correction), so total generation length grows monotonically.

verification.spec: Run the speculative decoding loop for a set number of iterations on several prompts (including adversarial ones where every candidate is rejected). After each iteration, assert len(output_tokens) strictly increased by at least 1. Fail if any iteration produces zero net tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: The outer speculative decoding loop correctly updates context and terminates.

Code has been implemented that appends all accepted tokens (plus any corrected/bonus token) to the running context s and repeats the draft/verify cycle until an EOS token or maximum length is reached.

verification.spec: Run end-to-end generation on a prompt with a small max_new_tokens. Verify (a) after each accept step, accepted tokens (plus corrected/bonus token) are appended to the context passed to the next iteration, and (b) generation halts when either an EOS token is emitted or max_new_tokens is reached. Test both termination paths by choosing prompts / max lengths that trigger each.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under greedy target decoding, the standard SD implementation produces exactly the same output sequence as running the target model autoregressively on the same prompt (deterministic distribution-preservation check for a fixed seed and identical prompt).

verification.spec: Fix the prompt 'The capital of France is' and greedy decoding (temperature=0, top_k=1). Generate 64 tokens with (a) plain target-only autoregressive decoding and (b) standard SD using an 8B drafter and the same target under greedy verification. Assert the two token sequences are identical.

sub_tasks.requirements: The judge decoding inference procedure — combining the standard SD accept mask with the judge accept mask via logical OR, using threshold δ=0.5 — is correctly implemented.
The judge accept mask is computed from the target model's last-layer token embeddings using the trained linear judge head.

Code has been implemented to extract the last hidden-layer embeddings (before the final RMSNorm and LM head) of the target model for each candidate token c_1, ..., c_M during the parallel verification forward pass.

verification.spec: Run a parallel verification forward pass on the target model with M candidate tokens. Confirm that the code taps the final transformer block output BEFORE the final RMSNorm and LM head, returning a tensor of shape (M+1, D) or (batch, M+1, D). Compare with a manual hook on the same layer and verify tensor equality (allclose).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to apply the linear judge head f_judge to each candidate-token embedding e_i to produce a scalar logit per token.

verification.spec: Given a batch of candidate-token embeddings e of shape (M, D), call the judge head and verify the output tensor has shape (M,) (scalar logit per token). Verify the head is a nn.Linear(D, 1) and its parameter count matches ~16.4k (for D~16384 hidden size of Llama-405B).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to convert judge logits into acceptance probabilities via the sigmoid function σ, matching the paper's definition σ(f_judge(e_i)).

verification.spec: Feed synthetic judge logits (e.g., [-10, 0, 10]) through the acceptance-probability computation and assert outputs equal torch.sigmoid of those logits within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a candidate token c_i is judge-accepted iff σ(f_judge(e_i)) > δ, producing the binary mask z_judge ∈ {0,1}^M.

verification.spec: For synthetic logits producing sigmoid values [0.4, 0.6, 0.51, 0.49, 0.95] with delta=0.5, assert z_judge equals [0,1,1,0,1]. Check that the mask is a torch.BoolTensor or int tensor of length M matching the number of candidates.

sub_tasks.requirements: The judge threshold δ defaults to 0.5 (as stated in Section 4.1), and is exposed as a configurable parameter in [0.5, 1] where δ=1 must reduce judge decoding to standard SD.

verification.spec: Inspect the judge decoding config/API and confirm delta defaults to 0.5. Confirm delta is a configurable float parameter, and that passing delta=1.0 disables judge acceptance (all judge outputs treated as rejects, so combined mask equals standard SD mask). Range assertions in [0.5, 1] should be enforced or documented.

sub_tasks.requirements: The judge mask and the standard-SD mask are combined via logical OR, and the effective accept prefix is derived correctly from the combined mask.
Code has been implemented that constructs the final mask z = z_stand ∨ z_judge as an elementwise logical OR of the standard SD mask and the judge mask, matching Section 4.1.

verification.spec: For synthetic z_stand=[1,0,1,0,1] and z_judge=[0,1,0,0,1], verify the combined-mask computation returns elementwise OR [1,1,1,0,1] (before any prefix truncation) using bitwise/logical OR.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that once both z_stand and z_judge disagree with acceptance at some position i (i.e., the combined mask has its first 0), all subsequent candidate tokens are rejected regardless of their individual mask values, as illustrated in Figure 7.

verification.spec: For combined mask [1,1,0,1,1], assert the effective accept prefix used by inference is length 2 (leading 1-run) and that candidates at positions 3,4 are discarded even though their combined-mask bit is 1. Verify via inspecting number-of-accepted-tokens returned.

sub_tasks.requirements: The number of accepted tokens m* returned per verification step equals the length of the leading 1-run in the combined mask z, and this value is used to advance the context by m* tokens (plus the bonus token where applicable).

verification.spec: Run one verification step with a mocked combined mask [1,1,1,0,1] and assert the returned m* equals 3 and that the context is advanced by 3 tokens (plus a bonus token in the all-accepted case). Assert that with mask [1,1,1,1,1] m*=M and one bonus token is sampled.

sub_tasks.requirements: Rejection handling and next-token sampling on rejection follow the SD rules while accounting for the merged mask, as described in Appendix B.2 and Figure 8.

Code has been implemented so that when the combined mask first rejects at position i, a corrected next token is sampled from the target distribution p_i (matching the SD fallback), and when all M candidates are accepted an additional bonus token is sampled from p_{M+1}.

verification.spec: With combined mask having first rejection at position i, verify the fallback token is drawn from target's p_i (greedy or multinomial depending on config) by mocking p_i as one-hot and checking the sampled token id matches. With all-accept mask, verify a bonus token is drawn from p_{M+1}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code correctly handles the Appendix B.2 corner case where the judge rejects a token but the standard SD mask accepts it (i.e., the target's corrected token equals the draft token), so that no redundant verification step is spent and the token is accepted in the same iteration.

verification.spec: Construct a case where z_judge[i]=0 but z_stand[i]=1, meaning standard SD accepts the draft token. Assert combined mask still accepts at position i (OR yields 1), so the token is kept and inference does NOT resample at position i (i.e., no extra target call is spent on that position).

sub_tasks.requirements: After each verification step the accepted tokens are appended to context s and the loop repeats with fresh drafting of M candidates until an EOS or max-length stopping criterion is met.

verification.spec: Run judge decoding end-to-end with a small max_new_tokens (e.g., 32) on a dummy prompt using a small model pair. Verify: (a) generation loop iterates multiple drafting rounds, (b) accepted tokens are appended to context between rounds, (c) loop terminates on EOS or when total generated tokens >= max_new_tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral checks confirm the judge inference procedure operates as specified on controlled inputs.

A unit test verifies that given a synthetic standard mask and judge mask, the combined accept prefix equals the leading 1-run of their elementwise OR (including the truncation-after-first-disagreement behavior of Figure 7).

verification.spec: Unit test: for random synthetic pairs (z_stand, z_judge) of length M, compute the reference accept prefix as len(leading 1-run of (z_stand | z_judge)) and compare against the implementation's returned m*. Run for at least 100 random cases and assert equality in all.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that when all judge sigmoid outputs are below 0.5, the combined mask equals the standard SD mask, and when all are above 0.5, the combined accept prefix covers all M candidates.

verification.spec: Unit test: (1) set judge logits so sigmoid < 0.5 for all M candidates and assert combined accept prefix equals leading 1-run of z_stand. (2) set judge logits so sigmoid > 0.5 for all M and assert combined accept prefix length equals M (all candidates accepted).

sub_tasks.requirements: The top-K training-free verification baseline (Section 5.1) is implemented as a relaxed acceptance scheme where a candidate token c_i is accepted if it lies among the K highest-probability target predictions given the previous token, providing a heuristic comparison point for judge decoding.
The top-K verification decision function is implemented as a separate acceptance mechanism.

Code has been implemented that, given a candidate token c_i drafted after context ending at c_{i-1}, computes the target model's softmax probability vector p_i over the vocabulary conditioned on the context up to c_{i-1}.

verification.spec: Feed context s and candidate tokens c_1..c_M through the target model's parallel forward pass. Verify the returned probability tensor has shape (M+1, V) and that softmax along vocab axis sums to 1 (within 1e-4). Cross-check p_i by running an autoregressive forward pass on context+c_1..c_{i-1} and comparing to allclose.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that accepts candidate token c_i if and only if c_i is among the top-K indices of the target probability vector p_i (i.e., its rank under p_i is <= K).

verification.spec: Construct synthetic p_i as a known distribution (e.g., probabilities [0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05]). For K=2, assert candidate token id=0 or 1 is accepted and id=2..4 is rejected. Repeat for varied K values and confirm acceptance corresponds exactly to topk(p_i, K) index set.

sub_tasks.requirements: The value K is exposed as a configurable hyperparameter of the decoding technique (integer input), controlling the speed-quality trade-off described in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Inspect the top-K decoding config/CLI: confirm K is an integer parameter, and that changing K between calls affects acceptance behavior (e.g., K=1 rejects more tokens than K=100 on a fixed prompt).

sub_tasks.requirements: The top-K scheme's boundary behavior matches the description in Section 5.1.
When K=1, the top-K verification reduces exactly to greedy standard speculative decoding (accepting only when the candidate equals the argmax of the target distribution), as stated in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Run top-K decoding with K=1 and greedy standard SD with same seed, prompt, draft, and target models. Assert generated token sequences match exactly and per-step m* counts are identical.

sub_tasks.requirements: When K equals the vocabulary size V, top-K verification accepts all draft tokens, effectively running only the draft model, as stated in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Run top-K decoding with K equal to the target vocabulary size V. Assert every candidate token is accepted for a small M=5 draft, so per-step m*=M+1 (all accepted plus bonus), and the resulting output matches what pure draft-model greedy generation would produce.

sub_tasks.requirements: The top-K baseline is integrated into the speculative decoding loop and evaluated on the benchmarks.

Code has been implemented that plugs the top-K acceptance rule into the speculative decoding verification step (in place of standard probability-ratio acceptance) while retaining draft generation and fallback token sampling on the first rejection.

verification.spec: Run top-K SD end-to-end on a small prompt with a small draft/target pair. Verify that (a) draft model produces M candidates each step, (b) verification uses topK acceptance rule (not probability-ratio), (c) on first rejection at position i a fallback token is sampled from target's p_i, and (d) generation terminates correctly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Top-K decoding is evaluated at multiple K values including at least K=5 (as explicitly referenced in Section 5.1) to support the claim that even K=5 hardly improves over the draft model.

verification.spec: Include K=5 in the top-K decoding evaluation sweep. On at least one benchmark (e.g., GSM8K or HumanEval) with Llama-8B/70B, verify that the K=5 accuracy is close to draft-only accuracy (within a few percentage points) and clearly below target accuracy, matching the paper's claim that even K=5 hardly improves over the draft model.

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured behavior of top-K verification matches the paper's qualitative claim about its limitations.

On the benchmarks in Fig. 6, top-K decoding with K=5 achieves benchmark accuracy that is close to the standalone Llama-8B draft model (i.e., hardly improves over the draft) and clearly below judge decoding, matching the observation in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Run top-K speculative decoding with K=5 using Llama-3.1-8B as draft and Llama-3.1-70B (or 405B) as target on HumanEval (and optionally GSM8K/MT-Bench). Measure the pass@1 accuracy. Verify that the resulting accuracy is close to the standalone Llama-3.1-8B draft model (~71.3% pass@1 on HumanEval per the paper) and clearly below judge decoding accuracy (~86% on HumanEval). The measurement checks that top-K=5 accuracy stays near draft baseline (within tolerance of 71.3%).

sub_tasks.requirements: The qualitative analysis showing that target embeddings flag errors when conditioned on wrong replies (Fig. 5 left, Fig. 12, Fig. 13) is reproduced, demonstrating that last hidden layer embeddings of erroneous tokens contain error-signal information that motivates the judge head design.
The forced-prefix conditioning experiment infrastructure that generates continuations from Llama-3.1-405B after prefilling incorrect assistant responses is implemented.

Code has been implemented to prompt Llama-3.1-405B with a user question and a partially-forced assistant response prefix (e.g., 'The capital of France is Berlin'), then allow the model to freely generate subsequent tokens conditioned on that forced prefix.

verification.spec: Import the forced-prefix generation utility; provide a user question and forced assistant prefix (e.g., 'The capital of France is Berlin'); confirm Llama-3.1-405B generates continuation tokens conditioned on that prefix (i.e., the prefix appears verbatim in output and further tokens follow).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to distinguish tokens in the forced prefix (highlighted red) from freely generated tokens (highlighted green) for visualization/analysis of the model's continuation behavior, matching the presentation style in Fig. 5 left.

verification.spec: Confirm the visualization code tags forced-prefix tokens vs freely-generated tokens with distinct labels/colors (e.g., red/green) and outputs a human-readable rendering in the style of Fig. 5 left.

sub_tasks.requirements: The specific qualitative prompts used in Fig. 5, Fig. 12, and Fig. 13 (capital-of-France, arithmetic 402+335, kilogram feathers-vs-stones, Python double_elements, odd_to_zero) are reproduced and the model's error-recovery continuations are collected.
Code has been implemented to run the 'capital of France is Berlin' forced-prefix prompt on Llama-3.1-405B and capture its continuation.

verification.spec: Run the specific 'capital of France is Berlin' forced-prefix prompt through Llama-3.1-405B. Confirm the model produces a non-empty continuation text.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to run the arithmetic forced-prefix prompt (e.g., '402 + 335 = 736') and the buggy Python function prompts from Fig. 12/13 through Llama-3.1-405B to observe error-flagging continuations.

verification.spec: Run the arithmetic ('402 + 335 = 736') and buggy Python function forced-prefix prompts from Figs. 5/12/13 through Llama-3.1-405B; confirm continuations are generated for each.

sub_tasks.requirements: The qualitative claim that Llama-3.1-405B, when conditioned on the incorrect prefix 'The capital of France is Berlin', generates a self-correcting continuation identifying Paris as the actual capital (Fig. 5 left) is reproduced.

verification.spec: Prompt Llama-3.1-405B with a user question about the capital of France, forced assistant prefix 'The capital of France is Berlin', then let it continue. Check that the continuation contains 'Paris' and self-corrects (e.g., contains a phrase like 'just kidding' or 'actually Paris' or similar retraction), matching Fig. 5 left qualitatively.

sub_tasks.requirements: The qualitative claim that Llama-3.1-405B, when conditioned on buggy code (e.g., triple instead of double, undefined variable 'j', or missing list copy), continues with text explicitly flagging or correcting the bug (Fig. 12, Fig. 13) is reproduced for at least one of the buggy-code prompts.

verification.spec: Force Llama-3.1-405B to start its assistant response with each of the three buggy-code prefixes from Fig. 12 and Fig. 13 (triple-instead-of-double list function; function using undefined variable 'j'; function omitting list-copy causing aliasing). Continue greedy generation for at least 200 tokens. For each of at least one of these three prompts, check via string/regex matching (or an LLM-judge) that the continuation explicitly flags the bug or provides a corrected version (e.g., contains phrases like 'bug', 'corrected version', 'just kidding', or produces the correct code).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to extract last-hidden-layer embeddings (pre-RMSNorm, pre-LM-head) from Llama-3.1-405B at the position of the forced incorrect tokens, so that the error-signal content of these embeddings can be inspected analogously to what is exploited by the judge head.

verification.spec: Import the extraction module and call it with a Llama-3.1-405B forward pass on a prompt+forced-wrong-suffix. Verify it returns a tensor of shape [seq_len, hidden_dim=16384] (or [num_forced_tokens, 16384]) taken from the last transformer block output BEFORE the final RMSNorm and BEFORE the LM head. Sanity check: the extracted tensor differs from the post-RMSNorm hidden state and, when passed through the model's own RMSNorm+LM head, reproduces the model's next-token logits (allclose within 1e-3).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compare model continuations between a correct-prefix control condition and a wrong-prefix condition on the same user question, demonstrating that error-flagging behavior arises specifically from the incorrect prefix rather than being generic.

verification.spec: Run the comparison script that, for a set of user questions, generates continuations under (a) a correct forced prefix and (b) a wrong forced prefix, using the same target model and identical decoding settings. Verify it outputs paired continuations per question and computes/logs a differential indicating that error-flagging text (e.g., 'just kidding', 'actually', 'correction', 'bug') appears in the wrong-prefix condition but not the correct-prefix condition for at least one example.
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.1, 'Token embeddings signal errors' + Fig. 5 left

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to present the qualitative results in a figure/log format matching Fig. 5 left, Fig. 12, and Fig. 13, showing user question, forced (red) prefix, and generated (green) correction text side by side.

verification.spec: Run the visualization script and check that it emits an artifact (PNG/PDF/HTML/markdown) for each example containing three labeled fields: 'User Question', a red-highlighted forced prefix, and a green-highlighted generated continuation. Verify artifact files exist and contain the expected color/formatting markers (ANSI codes, HTML spans with color attributes, or matplotlib text with red/green colors).

sub_tasks.requirements: The accuracy benchmark results (Fig. 6) are reproduced for Llama-8B/70B and Llama-8B/405B on GSM8K, HumanEval, MT-Bench, ARC, and MMLU, comparing draft, target, standard SD (M=10), top-K, and judge decoding (M=25); target-quality preservation is verified.
The evaluation harness runs all five benchmarks (GSM8K, HumanEval, MT-Bench, ARC, MMLU) across the required decoding configurations and reports task-appropriate accuracy metrics.
